plan.title: Liver drug treatment DE with strandedness QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples with raw gene-level counts from STAR/featureCounts (12000 genes x 6 samples), single batch, unpaired. Two data-quality concerns dominate the plan: (1) the library strandedness was never recorded, so a strand-setting error at the counting step could have mis-assigned or dropped reads for genes with an antisense-overlapping neighbor, which the standard sample-structure QC would not surface; (2) with only 3 replicates per group the test is underpowered per the replicate-count literature (Schurch et al. 2016), so absence from the significant list must not be read as evidence of no change. The plan therefore opens with a QC step that both runs the standard blind-VST/PCA/sample-distance diagnostic and adds a strandedness-consistency check built from the GENCODE annotation (genes with an antisense-overlapping neighbor should show a lopsided count ratio under a correctly stranded protocol and a near-1:1 ratio under an unstranded protocol; a mismatch between the assumed protocol and this pattern is reported as a caveat, not silently corrected, because the raw reads/BAMs needed for a true infer_experiment-style re-count are not available in this environment). Differential expression then follows the grounded DESeq2 Wald + apeglm shrinkage + BH/independent-filtering procedure, with an edgeR quasi-likelihood run in parallel as the required robustness check for a 3-vs-3 design, reporting the intersection as the high-confidence set. Enrichment runs preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (present in the reference store) with Reactome as the follow-up collection, respecting the >=50 significant-gene threshold rule for switching away from ORA. The final report consolidates DE tables, diagnostics, enrichment, and states the strandedness uncertainty and power limitation explicitly.
